authors: Claude Code session (holant lead, step b)

links.motivation: docs/reports/holant-step-b-qtt-20261104/README.md: the one curve where X fell below the null (p=61, a=21, b=57) has #E = p. That curve is excluded from this test and reported separately.
links.note: Confirmatory follow-up of a single post-hoc observation. Small primes (37..127) where QTT ranks are not saturated.

question: Over the primes 37 <= p <= 127, is the natural-labelling QTT complexity of the transfer matrix M, measured as a percentile within each curve's own random-relabelling null, lower for anomalous curves (#E = p) than for ordinary prime-order curves over the same primes?

claims.text: Anomalous curves have lower within-null percentile of X's QTT parameter count than ordinary prime-order curves (stratified by p), by the preregistered rule.
claims.if_supported: anomalous curves show digit-level structure in x-labelling that ordinary curves lack; next: mechanism (p-adic / formal-group structure) and a size ladder
claims.if_not_supported: the p=61 observation was chance; no anomalous-specific QTT structure at p <= 127

hypotheses.statement: The p=61 observation is chance: anomalous and ordinary curves have the same distribution of within-null percentiles.
hypotheses.mechanism: x-coordinates behave as pseudo-random labels for both families; anomaly (trace 1) is a property of the group order, not of the digit structure of x.

data_seen.measured: one anomalous curve at p=61 with X below its null; motivating curve excluded here

arms.description: natural x-labelling of M on anomalous curves (#E = p)
natural x-labelling of M on ordinary prime-order curves, same primes, matched count
99 uniform random relabellings per curve; draw 0 vs draws 1..98 is the A/A

positive.expected_detection: mean within-null percentile of LOG < 0.05 in each group

null_population.description: uniform random relabellings of F_p applied to the same M of the same curve
null_population.why_n: percentile resolution 1/99 per curve; the test aggregates 126 curves

factors.name: prime
factors.how: both families on every prime; permutation stratified by prime

factors.name: curve
factors.how: isomorphism classes ((a u^4, b u^6) orbit minimum); up to 4 anomalous classes per prime drawn by sha256(protocol_sha|pick|p), ordinary classes drawn by the same stream to match the count

factors.name: group_order
factors.how: #E recorded; anomalous #E = p, ordinary #E prime != p; the within-curve null controls support size

factors.name: factor_base
factors.value: floor(sqrt p) smallest x on E

factors.name: padding
factors.how: same for both families on a prime

factors.name: motivating_curve
factors.value: (61,21,57) and its isomorphism class excluded from the test

randomization.arm_order_reason: ranks are exact deterministic counts of a fixed matrix; execution order cannot change them (no clock, no state carried between arms)

seed_derivation.note: curve picks sha256(protocol_sha|pick|p); null draws sha256(protocol_sha|anull|p|a|b|draw); permutation test seed 20261104 (fixed in analyze_anomalous.py)

instance_sampling.rule: curves chosen per prime before and independently of any rank computation

blinding.how: analysis is a frozen script applying a fixed rule; no analyst choice remains

power.note: 63 anomalous vs 63 ordinary curves, stratified label permutation with 9999 resamples; an effect like the p=61 curve (u about 0.03 against 0.5) would be detected with high power; a small shift (delta u < 0.1) may not be

preflight_runtime.measured_on: this container; one p=127 curve, 101 matrices, 0.9 s; curve picking 3.3 s; non-sample seed tag

primary.name: within-null percentile of X's QTT parameter count
primary.definition: mid-rank percentile of X's interleaved sum of log2 ranks among the curve's 99 null draws
primary.formula: u_X = (#{null log2_params < X log2_params} + 0.5 #{null log2_params == X log2_params}) / 99

secondary.name: within-null percentile of X's max interleaved rank
secondary.formula: u_X = (#{null r_max < X r_max} + 0.5 #{null r_max == X r_max}) / 99

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design: 126 curves x 101 matrices, then stop; motivating curve run afterwards with --include-excluded and reported only

decision_rule.text: Validity: mean u_LOG < 0.05 in each group and pooled mean u_AA in [0.35, 0.65], else INVALID_CONTROLS. EFFECT iff the one-sided stratified permutation p < 0.01 and mean u_X(anomalous) < 0.25. NULL iff p >= 0.05. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. C-aa is a validity gate.

inadmissible: changing primes, per-group caps, FB rule, null draws or the decision rule after seeing results
including the motivating curve in the test
reading EFFECT as an attack-cost claim
